=== tmux-persist-daemon script ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Persistent tmux autosave daemon.
#
# Why this replaces the plugin's status-bar trigger:
# continuum normally schedules saves by putting `#(continuum_save.sh)` in
# status-right and relying on status-interval to re-evaluate it. But status
# options are only expanded when a client actually DRAWS the status bar. With
# no client attached -- which is the normal state for a persistent, detached
# setup -- nothing ever expands it, so no save ever happens. That is why the
# newest snapshot sat at 2026-07-17 for over two months.
#
# This loop is independent of clients: it runs from tmux server start (see
# ~/.dracon/nixos/terminal/tmux.conf) and keeps saving whether or not anyone
# is looking.
#
# Single-instance guarded by a pidfile, so reloading the tmux config does not
# spawn duplicates. The save script applies its own 5-minute gate, so calling
# it every 60s is cheap and guarantees a save lands within ~6 minutes of a
# change.

set -u

INTERVAL="${TMUX_PERSIST_INTERVAL:-60}"
PIDFILE="${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/tmux-persist-$$.pid"

# Which server this daemon serves. `run-shell -b` from a tmux.conf sets $TMUX
# to that server's socket, so each server gets its own daemon; without $TMUX
# fall back to the default socket. All tmux calls go through `t` so a stale
# environment can never aim this daemon at the wrong server.
SOCKPATH="${TMUX:-}"
SOCKPATH="${SOCKPATH%%,*}"
if [ -z "$SOCKPATH" ]; then
    SOCKPATH="${TMUX_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/tmux-$(id -u)/default"
fi
t() { tmux -S "$SOCKPATH" "$@"; }

# No server on our socket (scratch server gone, socket file stale): exit
# instead of idling forever as a zombie that trims nothing.
t list-sessions >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0

# Single-instance guard, one per socket.
#
# The original keyed the lock on `tmux display-message -p '#{pid}'`, which is
# the CLIENT pid -- and it is empty when nothing is attached. Every detached
# start therefore computed the same (useless) key and `mkdir` succeeded again,
# so a rebuild left nine daemons running. Key on the socket instead: it is
# stable for the lifetime of a server and identical across all clients.
#
# Two more fixes in this guard. The EXIT trap used to be armed BEFORE the lock
# was acquired, so a duplicate that found the lock held and exited via `exit 0`
# ran cleanup and DELETED the live owner's lock -- every config reload then
# added another daemon, which is how five ended up running with no lock at
# all. And a contender that found the lock held but the pid file not yet
# written stole the lock from a winner mid-startup. Now the trap is armed only
# after acquiring, cleanup removes the lock only if we own it, and an empty
# pid means "freshly claimed, back off".
SOCKKEY="$(printf '%s' "$SOCKPATH" | cksum | cut -d' ' -f1)"
LOCK="/tmp/tmux-persist-$(id -u)-${SOCKKEY}.lock"

if ! mkdir "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null; then
